findings.resolution: Include orchestrator/item4_fit_transport_recovery.py and orchestrator/item4_closed_attempt_billing.py (and their tests) in the review packet so the reservation-release and billing-confirmation logic can be inspected against the operator rule: release excess only after provider billing confirms the actual cost of a CLOSED attempt, and never release for an attempt still open or uncertain.
findings.text: The core behavior of this commit ('reconcile one positively stopped attempt') lives in a new module, orchestrator/item4_fit_transport_recovery.py (203 lines per the diff stat), which is invoked by the in-scope modal_terminal_cost.py at record() (lines 104-109: recovery.require/contract/saved_cost) and effective() (lines 151-153: fit_recovery). That module, plus item4_closed_attempt_billing.effective (lines 155-157), carries the actual decision of how much reservation is released and whether billing is confirmed. Neither module is in the review scope and neither is present in the workspace, so the credit/release correctness that this change exists to perform cannot be independently verified.

findings.evidence: review/source/orchestrator/modal_terminal_cost.py:151-168 (line 153-154 returns fit_amount with no actual floor vs 157/159/168 using max(...,actual_micro_usd)); operator rule in source/docs/ITEM4_SMOKE_RETRY_OPERATOR_DECISION_20261009.txt ('record the actual cost and release the excess reservation ... never release a reservation for an attempt that is still open or uncertain').
findings.resolution: Either expose item4_fit_transport_recovery.effective for inspection to confirm it internally guarantees >= confirmed billed actual (and that the attempt is closed, not uncertain), or apply the same max(..., row['actual_micro_usd'] or 0) floor on the fit_recovery branch so the conservative invariant held by all other branches is visibly preserved.
findings.text: In modal_terminal_cost.effective(), the fit_recovery branch returns fit_amount verbatim (line 153-154) with no max(..., row['actual_micro_usd']) floor, unlike every sibling branch: closed_billing uses max(reconciled, actual) (157), the no-record branch uses max(reserved, actual) (159), and the terminal-exposure branch uses max(bound, actual) (168). Because the amount is produced entirely by the out-of-scope item4_fit_transport_recovery.effective, it cannot be confirmed that the released/effective cost is never below confirmed provider billing for this attempt. The operator reconciliation rule requires recording the actual cost and only releasing the excess; a path that bypasses the conservative actual-cost floor present everywhere else is a potential budget/under-billing risk that is not independently verifiable in scope.

rationale: Independent judgment: The listed in-scope files (modal_terminal_cost.py, modal_item4_budget.py, item4_closed_asset_billing.py, modal_item4_policy.py, experiment_projection.py) are internally self-consistent and preserve the $75 smoke cap (SMOKE_CAP=75_000_000) and conservative max(reserved,actual) accounting in most paths; the asset_effective call signature and observe_billing ordering in the budget module are consistent. However, this commit's stated purpose is to 'reconcile one positively stopped attempt,' and the actual release/credit and billing-confirmation logic resides in orchestrator/item4_fit_transport_recovery.py (new, 203 lines) and item4_closed_attempt_billing.py, which are invoked by the changed modal_terminal_cost.py but are outside the review scope and absent from the workspace. The operator's money rule is strict and non-delegable (release excess only on confirmed billing of a CLOSED attempt; never for open/uncertain). Whether this change honors that rule depends entirely on uninspectable code, and the fit_recovery branch in effective() uniquely omits the actual-cost floor applied on every other branch. Missing inspection of the determinative modules, on a budget-affecting reconciliation, mandates a non-APPROVE verdict. I do not reach a final PROCEED/SIMPLIFY/ASK recommendation on the second-opinion framing because the code required to judge safety was not provided; the correct next step is to widen the packet to include the recovery/closed-attempt billing modules and their tests, then re-review.
